title: Which Stretch of the Ledger the Measured Balance Is Taken Over
content:
Where a spending restriction has stood on an Employee Meal Account for some time, the balance the paydown is measured on is taken over a stretch of the account's ledger that follows how long the restriction has run and whether a recovery has lately been remitted.

**Clause.** Where the account has stood restricted for longer than twice the grace days printed against the plan and a recovery has been remitted on it in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, the measured balance is the charges accrued in the three calendar months running back from the day the account is worked less the recoveries remitted in those same three months. Where the account has stood restricted for longer than twice those grace days and no recovery has been remitted on it in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, the measured balance is the charges accrued in the twelve calendar months running back from the day the account is worked less the recoveries remitted in those same twelve months. Where neither holds, the measured balance is every charge accrued to date less every recovery remitted to date.

In each case the recoveries are netted against the charges over the very same stretch, and the figure is never read as less than nothing.

## The grace days this reads, plan by plan

| Meal plan | Grace after the arrears threshold is passed |
|---|---|
| Pay-As-You-Go Badge Account | 0 calendar days |
| Prepaid Declining Balance Account | 0 calendar days |
| Payroll Deduction Meal Account | 10 calendar days |
| Subsidized Daily Allowance Account | 7 calendar days |
| Full Subsidy Employee Meal Account | 0 calendar days |
| Executive Dining Charge Account | 21 calendar days |

Twice those grace days is therefore 20 calendar days on the Payroll Deduction Meal Account, 14 on the Subsidized Daily Allowance Account and 42 on the Executive Dining Charge Account; on the three plans printing 0 calendar days of grace, twice nothing is nothing, so any restriction that has stood for a day at all has stood longer than it.

## The three stretches

| Days the restriction has stood | A recovery remitted in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked | Charges and recoveries summed over |
|---|---|---|
| More than twice the printed grace days | Yes | The three calendar months running back from the day the account is worked |
| More than twice the printed grace days | No | The twelve calendar months running back from the day the account is worked |
| Twice the printed grace days or fewer | Either | The whole ledger to date |

*Hypothetical illustration.* On a plan printing 10 calendar days of grace, a restriction standing 21 days is past twice that figure; a restriction standing exactly 20 days is not, and the measured balance is then taken over the whole ledger.
